It depends on what one does, not on what one says. If a man's activities do result in mischief, he will be called a mischief-maker, even if he had no such intention.

**Corruption dressed as reform.**

But the miscreants who have been described in these verses always appear in the garb of reformers, brandishing colourful schemes of social amelioration which are only a mask for personal interests, and for raising the slogan, :"We are nothing but reformers. " Hence it is that Allah, while asking men not to spread disorder on the earth, has also said in another place: They call their own policy, on the other hand, one of reform; they prize it because it enables them to pursue a safe course without clashing with anyone; but this just shows how distorted their reasoning is. If they were to think deeply, they would realize that on earth reform can only come from man giving himself up to God alone, while obstructing any movement aimed at consolidating man’s relationship with the will of his Lord amounts to creating disorder on earth. (And when it is said unto them), i.e. the Jews (Make not mischief in the land) by preventing people from the Religion of Muhammad ﷺ (they say: we are reformers only), we are reforming it through obedience.

12.text:
This short verse answers the claim made in the verse before, that they were only peace-makers. "Indeed, it is they who are the corruptors" opens with a word meant to make the hearer stop and pay attention, and then turns their own phrase back on them. They had claimed to be nothing but reformers, and the reply is that they, and no one else, are the ones spreading corruption. Their deceit is itself corruption, because they confuse the believers by claiming a faith they do not have, and because they help the enemies of the believers in secret. "but they fail to perceive it" repeats the note heard a few verses earlier, when they deceived only themselves without perceiving it. They do not see their own behaviour for what it is. They avoided the obvious crimes that everyone recognises, and so they told themselves they were innocent, while they spread envy, malice and doubt that harm a community more deeply than theft. The verse teaches that harm does not stop being harm because the one doing it does not intend it or does not notice it. What matters is the effect of a person's deeds, measured by God's command, and not his opinion of himself. It also shows how far the hypocrite is from being cured, since he cannot repent of a corruption he will not admit. The next verse moves from their deeds to their opinion of the believers.

**Why they are the mischief-makers.**

Hence, the deceitful behavior of the hypocrites is an act of mischief, because they deceive the believers by claiming what they do not believe in, and because they give support and loyalty to the disbelievers against the believers. This Ayah means that the hypocrites' behavior, and their claim that it is for peace, is itself mischief, although in their ignorance, they do not see it to be mischief. (They are indeed the mischief mongers) by being a hindrance. The truth is that it is they who ruin things, but they do not admit this, nor do they know that their actions are the cause of all ruin. Truly a-lā ‘truly’ is for alerting intended emphatically they are the agents of corruption but they perceive this not.

**Spreading disorder without being aware of it.**

Firstly, the activities of the hypocrites did actually produce disorder in the land. Secondly, they did not indulge in these activities with the express intention or design of creating disorder they were not even aware of the possibility that their actions could be the cause of disorder. For, among the things which spread disorder in the world, there are some which are commonly recognized to be mischievous and disorderly activities, and hence every sensible and conscientious man refrains from them e.g., theft, robbery, murder, rape etc.; on the other hand, there are some which in their external aspect do not appear to be mischief or disorder, but, working unseen, they have the necessary consequence of destroying the morals of men which, in its turn, opens the door to all kinds of disorder. No doubt, they refrained from theft, robbery etc.; it was on this count that they denied their being mischievous, and emphatically asserted that they were serving the cause of order. But all this while they had been freely giving vent to their malice and envy by conspiring with the enemies of the Muslims. (But they perceive not): the followers do not know that their leaders mislead them.

**The hypocrite's harm, and the way out of it.**

Since the outward appearance of the hypocrite displays belief, he confuses the true believers. If the hypocrite remains a disbeliever (rather than pretending to be Muslim), the evil that results from him would be less. Even better, if the hypocrite becomes sincere with Allah and makes the statements that he utters conform to his deeds, he will gain success. The hypocrites also lie to the believers by saying contrary to the doubt and hesitation their hearts harbor. It is said that it is sufficient to expose those who lie by saying to such a person's face You have lied.

13.text:
The verse shows a second side of the hypocrites, how they looked down on the believers. "And when they are told" means whenever they were urged by the believers to stop their double dealing and to accept the faith sincerely. What they were told was "Believe as others believe, they reply", and the others here are the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, the people who had truly accepted the faith. The call is not only to believe but to believe in the same way they did, in God, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Resurrection, with obedience to His commands. Their faith is set up as the measure for everyone else's. The hypocrites answer with contempt, "Will we believe as the fools believe? Indeed, it is they who are fools". They call the believers fools, people who are simple, easily led and ready to give up their worldly comfort for a promise they cannot see. This has always been the way of those who go astray. Whoever tries to show them the right path looks foolish to them, and their own cleverness looks like wisdom. The answer comes straight back, in the very next words: it is they who are the fools. A fool is someone who does not know what benefits him and what harms him, and no one fits that better than a person who sees clear signs and still chooses to lose both this world and the next. The verse ends "but they do not know". This is the third time in a few verses that their ignorance of their own state is named. They deceived themselves without perceiving it, they spread corruption without perceiving it, and now they are fools without knowing it. That kind of ignorance is the most dangerous kind, since a person who knows he is ignorant may learn, while a person who thinks he is wise will not. The next verse shows how they behaved when they were with the believers and when they were not.

**Believe as the people believe.**

("Believe as the people believe,"), meaning, 'Believe just as the believers believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, Resurrection after death, Paradise and Hellfire, etc. And obey Allah and His Messenger by heeding the commandments and avoiding the prohibitions.' Yet the hypocrites answer by saying,. This verse also places before the hypocrites a criterion of true faith (Iman) :"Believe as people have believed". (people) in this verse refers to the blessed Companions of the Holy Prophet because it is just these 'people' who had embraced the Faith and had accepted the Holy Qur'an as the word of Allah while it was being revealed. When it is said to them ‘Believe as the people believe’ that is as the Companions of the Prophet s They say ‘Shall we believe as fools believe?’ that is as the ignorant do? When they are told to have faith as the companions of Muhammad ﷺ did, they reply, looking down on people and making fun of them, saying “should we have faith like simple-minded people do?

**The faith of the Companions as the measure.**

So, the verse indicates that the only kind of Iman (faith) acceptable to Allah is the one which should be similar to that of the blessed Companions, and that the Iman of others would be worthy of the name only when they believe in the same things in the same way as the Companions did. In other words, the Iman of the Companions is a touchstone for testing the Iman of all the other Muslims; any belief. or deed which departs from their faith and practice, however pleasing in its looks or good in its intention, is not valid according to the Shari ah. There is a consensus of commentators on this position. (And when it is said unto them) i.e. to Jews, (believe) in Muhammad ﷺ (as the people believe), i.e. 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his companions, (they say: Shall we believe) in Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an, (as the foolish believe?), i.e. as the stupid and ignorant do, (Surely they are the fools) the stupid and ignorant.

**Why they called the believers fools.**

("Shall we believe as the fools have believed?") they meant (may Allah curse the hypocrites) the Companions of the Messenger of Allah . The hypocrites said, "Us and them having the same status, following the same path, while they are fools?!" 'The fool' is the ignorant, simple-minded person who has little knowledge in areas of benefit and harm. This is why, according to the majority of the scholars, Allah used the term foolish to include children, when He said,. One should also notice that the hypocrites used to call the blessed Companions 'fools' (Sufaha-'). This has always been the way of those who go astray - anyone who tries to show them the right path is, in their eyes, ignorant and stupid. But who could, the Holy Qur'an points out, be more stupid than the man who refuses to see clear signs?

**It is they who are the fools, the foolish and ignorant.**

Allah answered the hypocrites in all of these instances. Allah thus affirmed that the hypocrites are indeed the fools, yet,. Since they are so thoroughly ignorant, the hypocrites are unaware of their degree of deviation and ignorance, and such situation is more dangerous, a severer case of blindness, and further from the truth than one who is aware. The exalted One refutes them saying Truly they are the foolish ones but they know this not. ” In fact, it is they who are the fools, but they are unaware of this.

**How hypocrites are recognised now.**

At that time, there were two ways of identifying a hypocrite and declaring him to be one -either Allah Himself informed the Holy Prophet through revelation that such and such a man was not a Muslim at heart but a hypocrite, or a man through some word or deed overtly repugnant to the Islamic creed or practice showed himself up as a hypocrite, thus providing a clear evidence against himself. Divine revelation having ceased with the departure of the Holy Prophet from this world, the first way of identifying a hypocrite is no longer available, but the second way is still valid. One must also add that since the kufr (infidelity) of such a man has been proved by clear and definite evidence, the Shari'ah will not put him in a separate category, but deal with him as it would deal with any other kafir (infidel). That is why the authentic scholars are unanimous in concluding that after the departure of the Holy Prophet the question of hypocrites ceased to be a relevant one - now anyone who is not a genuine Muslim will be regarded as kafir .

**The worthy and the unworthy.**

The stamp of worthiness is upon some people, and the brand of unworthiness on others. The worthy are brought by the road of bounty on the steed of approval with the escort of gentleness in the time of generous bestowal at the turn of proximity. The unworthy are driven into the street of justice on the steed of wrath with the escort of abandonment at the turn of deprivation. The purifiers, the truthful, and the Messenger's Com panions they called "fools. "Those are not the fools, the fools are those who call them fools.

14.text:
The verse lays out the hypocrites' two faces side by side. "When they meet the believers they say, We believe" describes the first face. In the company of the Muslims they declared their faith loudly and acted as friends and supporters. They did this to mislead the believers, and to take a share of whatever the believers gained, while committing themselves to nothing. "But when alone with their evil associates they say" turns to the second face. The evil associates are their leaders and masters in disbelief, the ones who directed them. The word used is the word for devils, and it covers the wicked among people as well as among the jinn, anyone who leads others into rebellion against God. Alone with these leaders, they say "We are definitely with you", meaning we are on your side and of your religion. Then they explain away what they had told the believers: "we were only mocking". Their words of faith had been, by their own account, a joke at the believers' expense, a way of fooling them. The two halves of the verse together show what hypocrisy is. It is not a confused heart that wavers honestly but a calculated performance, with one speech for one audience and another for the other. It also shows the end of that path. Someone who tries to belong to both sides ends up belonging to neither, trusted by no one and without a firm place to stand. An occasion is recorded for this verse, involving the leader of the hypocrites in Madīnah and some of the Companions, which is set out below. The next verse gives God's answer to their mockery.

**Their words when they meet the believers.**

Allah said that when the hypocrites meet the believers, they proclaim their faith and pretend to be believers, loyalists and friends. They do this to misdirect, mislead and deceive the believers. The hypocrites also want to have a share of the benefits and gains that the believers might possibly acquire. When the hypocrites meet the believers, they say, ‘We believe what you believe’, as they think it will benefit them if they act like this; but when they are alone with their leaders, they say, ‘We are really with you and follow you. Abu Bakr and his companions, (they say: We believe) deep in our hearts and are genuine in our faith just as you believe deep in your hearts and are genuine in your faith; (but when they go apart to their devils), to their soothsayers and leaders who were five in number, namely, Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf in Medina, Abu Burdah al-Aslami in Banu Aslam, Ibn al-Sawda' in Historic Syria (al-Sham), 'Abd al-Dar in Juhaynah and 'Awf Ibn 'Amir in Banu 'Amir, (they declare) to their leaders:

**Who their devils, the Shayatin, are.**

(But when they are alone with their Shayatin), meaning, if they are alone with their devils, such as their leaders and masters among the rabbis of the Jews, hypocrites and idolators. Ibn Jarir said, "The devils of every creation are the mischievous among them. (And so We have appointed for every Prophet enemies Shayatin (devils) among mankind and Jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech as a delusion (or by way of deception)(6:112). When they meet laqū is actually laquyū but the damma has been omitted being too cumbersome for pronunciation; likewise the yā’ is omitted because it is unvocalised and is followed by a wāw; those who believe they say ‘We believe’; but when they go apart away from them and return to their devils their leaders they say ‘We are with you in religion; we were only mocking them the believers by feigning belief.

**We were only mocking the believers and the Companions.**

(Verily, we were but mocking), meaning, we only mock people (the believers) and deceive them. (Verily, we were but mocking), means, "We (meaning the hypocrites) were mocking the Companions of Muhammad. (Lo! We are with you) we follow your religion in secret; (surely we did but mock) Muhammad ﷺ and his Companions. We are only making fun of them when we say that we believe’.

**Revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy.**

This verse was revealed about 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his followers. It so happened that they went out one day and were received by a group of Companions of Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: 'See how I will bar these fools from you!' He proceeded and took hold of the hand of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be well pleased with him, and said: 'Welcome to the truthful, the master of Banu Tamim and leader of Islam, the second person in the cave along with Allah's Messenger, who gave up his person and his wealth'. Then he took hold of the hand of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be well pleased with him, and said: 'Welcome to the master of Banu 'Adiyy ibn Ka'b, the distinguisher and the strong in the religion of Allah, who gave up his person and wealth for Allah's Messenger'. Then he took hold of the hand of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah ennoble his face, and said: 'Welcome to the cousin and son-in-law of Allah's Messenger, the master of Banu Hashim apart from Allah's Messenger'. But when the Muslims returned to the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, and informed him of what happened, Allah revealed this verse .

**Why their claim of faith was refused.**

A little reflection on these verses would reveal the true nature of Islam and Iman (faith) and also that of kufr (disbelief), for the Holy Qur'an reports the claim of the hypocrites to be Muslims: :"we believe in Allah", , forthwith refutes this claim: :"yet they are no believers". Now, belief in Allah and in Hereafter is, no doubt, an essential part of their creed as well; what was not included in their creed, as defined by their religious scholars, was the belief in the prophethood of Muhammad . In declaring their faith in Islam, the Jews very cleverly used to leave out the belief in the Holy Prophet and mention only two elements: belief in Allah and belief in the Hereafter. So far as such a declaration goes, they cannot be called liars, and yet the Holy Qur'an refutes their claim to be Muslims, and regards them as liars. Iman or faith in Allah must, in order to be valid and worthy of the name, conform to what the Holy Qur'an specifically lays down with regards to the divine names and attributes; similarly, belief in the Hereafter can be valid only when it is true to the specifications of the Holy Qur'an and the Hadith.7.

**Wanting relations with both sides, and belonging to neither.**

The hypocrites wanted to maintain their relations with disbelievers while associating with Muslims so when they appeared before Muslims they said We are with you and when they were alone with those like them among the disbelievers they voiced their loyalty to them. They wanted to have relationships with both sides but they were excluded from both. God most high said Wavering all the time-not to these neither to those [4:143]. Anyone who has a hodgepodge khalīṬ in every corner nāḥiyya and a heart bound rabīṬ in every nook zāwiyya is headed for disaster. First one group and then another take turns dwelling in his heart so that it is forever ruined.53 There is no pleasure for him in life nor does he truly possess any provision from his heart.

15.text:
This verse is the answer to the hypocrites' boast that they were only mocking the believers. "Allah will throw their mockery back at them" means that God repays their mockery in kind. They mocked the believers, and the result of that mockery returns on themselves. The verse uses the same word for the deed and for its repayment, but the two are not alike in nature. Their mockery was injustice and play at the expense of others, while God's repayment is justice, a fitting punishment for what they did. In this world they are treated as believers and left alone, and they take that as a sign that their trick has worked, while in the Hereafter they will see the truth of their position, and the treatment they received here will turn out to have been part of their ruin. "leaving them to continue wandering blindly in their defiance" describes how the repayment works. God gives them time. He does not punish them at once but lets them go on, and they use the time only to go further in their rebellion. Defiance here means going beyond every limit, the way flood water rises above its banks. Wandering blindly describes people lost in confusion, unable to see the way out, because they closed their own eyes to guidance. The respite they mistake for safety is the very thing that is destroying them. The verse warns that being left alone by God is not always a mercy. Someone who goes on sinning and sees no immediate harm may think he has nothing to fear, while each day added to his life increases what he will answer for. The next verse sums up their whole bargain in the language of trade.

**How God mocks them and repays their mockery.**

(Allah mocks at them and leaves them increasing in their deviation to wander blindly) answers the hypocrites and punishes them for their behavior. God Himself mocks them requiting them for their mockery leaving them that is giving them respite in their insolence that is in their transgressing the limits of unbelief; bewildered wavering in perplexity ya‘mahūn is a circumstantial qualifier. Allah mocks the hypocrites for their mocking of the believers, and He will repay in equal measure for their behavior. They are treated as believers in this world, but will be repaid for their lying and deception in the next life. (Allah (Himself) doth mock them), in the Hereafter, i.e. He will open a gate of Paradise for them and then shut it before their eyes and so the believers will mock them.

**The same term for the deed and its punishment.**

Allah stated that He will punish the hypocrites for their mockery, using the same terms to describe both the deed and its punishment, although the meaning is different. The first act is an act of injustice, while the second act is an act of justice. So both actions carry the same name, while being different in reality. This is how the scholars explain deceit, cunning and mocking when attributed to Allah in the Qur'an. Surely, Allah exacts revenge for certain evil acts with a punishment that is similar in nature to the act itself. We should affirm here that Allah does not do these things out of joyful play, according to the consensus of the scholars, but as a just form of punishment for certain evil acts. Allah acted like this in response to their mockery; so, the Holy Qur'an describes this divine action too as a mockery on the part of Allah.

**Leaving them to continue, a respite.**

(and leaves them increasing) means, He gives them respite. Also, Mujahid said, "He (causes their deviation) to increase. Ibn Jarir commented, "The correct meaning of this Ayah is 'We give them increase from the view of giving them respite and leaving them in their deviation and rebellion.' Similarly, Allah said,. (And let not the disbelievers think that Our postponing of their punishment is good for them. We postpone the punishment only so that they may increase in sinfulness.)(3:178)." For Allah has, in His forbearance and mercy, given them a long rope, but this is a provision for their being thrown into ridicule. Since the hypocrites saw no apparent signs of divine punishment descending on themselves, they were encouraged in their complacency and rebellion, so that the cup of their iniquity was full, and one day they were caught.

**Wandering blindly in their defiance.**

Tughyan used in this Ayah means to transgress the limits, just as Allah said in another Ayah,. Also, Ibn Jarir said that the term 'Amah, in the Ayah means, 'deviation'. (in their deviation to wander), "In the misguidance and disbelief that has encompassed them, causing them to be confused and unable to find a way out of it. This is because Allah has stamped their hearts, sealed them, and blinded their vision. Therefore, they do not recognize guidance or find the way out of their deviation." (Leaving them to wander blindly on in their contumacy) He will leave them in this world blind in their disbelief and error, unable to see either faith or guidance. He allows them to become more and more lost and to do more and more wrong, so they remain confused and doubtful about the truth.

**Confused hopes, and the worst of punishments.**

When the hypocrites said we were only mocking God most high said God [Himself] mocks them that is He requites them for their mocking. Just as he leaves the hypocrites in their insolence bewildered he prolongs the period [in which they dwell with] their confused hopes. So when the times of their deaths draw nigh their hopes are at their highest while their actions are at their lowest. The beautification of their ugly acts in their eyes is the worst of their punishments and their being content with their listlessness is their greatest misfortune.

16.text:
The verse sums up the hypocrites' whole course in the language of buying and selling. "They are the ones who trade guidance for misguidance" describes their choice as a bargain. Guidance was in their hands. They had seen the truth of the faith, many had professed it, and they knew the way of disbelief from their own past. Yet, out of greed and for the sake of small worldly gains, they gave guidance away and took misguidance in exchange. Some of them believed and then disbelieved, and others simply preferred error when guidance was offered to them, and both are included in the description. The image of trade is pointed. These were people who prided themselves on being shrewd in worldly affairs, and the verse shows that they did not understand even the first rule of trading, which is not to give away something precious for something worthless. "But this trade is profitless" states the result. A trader hopes to come away with more than he gave, but they came away with less. They lost the guidance they had and gained nothing that lasts. "and they are not rightly guided" closes the verse with a further loss. Not only did their trade fail, they did not even know how to trade, and they are not on the right path in anything they do. A merchant who loses money may at least learn from his mistake, but they have no guidance left to learn by. The verse puts a question to every reader about what he is exchanging his days and his faith for. The next verses turn the same lesson into two vivid pictures, first of a fire and then of a storm.

**What it means to trade guidance for misguidance.**

(These are they who have purchased error with guidance) saying it means, "They pursued misguidance and abandoned guidance. " Mujahid said, "They believed and then disbelieved," while Qatadah said, "They preferred deviation to guidance. In summary, the statements that we have mentioned from the scholars of Tafsir indicate that the hypocrites deviate from the true guidance and prefer misguidance, substituting wickedness in place of righteousness. (These are they who have purchased error with guidance), meaning, they exchanged guidance to buy misguidance. This meaning includes those who first believed, then later disbelieved, whom Allah described,. The Ayah also includes those who preferred deviation over guidance.

**Why the bargain is called trade, and the worldly profit.**

They had grown up in a pagan society, and knew very well what the way of the infidels was. Now they had become familiar enough with Islam too, and could easily see the difference. But, in their greed, and for the sake of petty worldly profit, they still chose disbelief as against Islam, and bartered away something as invaluable as Iman (faith) for something as worthless, and even harmful as kufr (infidelity). In giving the name of 'trade' or 'commerce' to this action, the Holy Qur'an suggests that these worldly-wise men had no understanding even of the art of trading.

**Their commerce was profitless.**

Those are they who have bought error for guidance that is they have exchanged the latter for the former; so their commerce has not profited them that is to say they have gained nothing from it indeed they have lost because their destination is the Fire made everlasting for them; nor are they guided in what they did. (So their commerce was profitless. And they were not guided), meaning their trade did not succeed nor were they righteous or rightly guided throughout all this. I have seen them leaving guidance for deviation, leaving the Jama'ah (the community of the believers) for the sects, leaving safety for fear, and the Sunnah for innovation. (These are they who purchase error at the price of guidance), they chose disbelief instead of faith and exchanged guidance with error, (so their commerce did not prosper), they did not prosper in their bargain but on the contrary (neither were they guided) to overcome their error. It is they who are the fools, because they exchanged faith for disbelief; and this exchange did not help them in any way, because they lost their faith in Allah and lost the way to the truth.

**Loss in this world and the next.**

This alludes to those who have neglected what is due ḥuqūq by remain ing in the familiar territories of worldly fortunes ḥuẓūẓ. [They] have lost their bargain so their commerce has not profited them. Those who are content with this world over the next are in manifest loss. Those who prefer this world or the next over the Real have the most intense loss.

17.text:
The verse begins the first of two parables about the hypocrites, and it is built like a short story. "Their example is that of someone who kindles a fire" sets the scene: a man in the dark lights a fire. "but when it lights up all around them" gives the moment of hope. He can see, he feels warm, and he feels safe from what he feared in the darkness. Then comes the turn, "Allah takes away their light". The light goes out, not by chance but by God's act, and what was given is withdrawn. "leaving them in complete darkness" describes the result, and it is worse than before the fire was lit, since now he had hoped for light and lost it. The darkness stands for their doubt, disbelief and hypocrisy. The verse ends "unable to see", lost, confused about the way, and afraid. Each part of the story matches the hypocrites. They lit a fire when they professed faith. For a time it gave them light: they were treated as Muslims, their lives and property were safe, and they shared in the community's benefits. But it was a light that did not reach their hearts, and when it was taken away, at the latest at death, they were left in a darker place than if they had never professed anything at all. The parable fits especially those whose disbelief was rooted deep, who had glimpsed the truth and then turned from it. The second parable, which begins two verses later, describes a different kind of hypocrite, one who hesitates between belief and disbelief. When these parables came down, some objected that God was too exalted to coin such examples, and that objection is answered later in the chapter. The next verse completes this first parable with the state they are left in.

**The parable of the one who kindles a fire.**

Allah likened the hypocrites when they bought deviation with guidance, thus acquiring utter blindness, to the example of a person who started a fire. When the fire was lit, and illumnitated the surrounding area, the person benefited from it and felt safe. Therefore, total darkness covered this person, and he became unable to see anything or find his way out of it. Their likeness the way they are in their hypocrisy is as the likeness of one who kindled that is one who lit a fire in darkness and when it illumined all about him so that he is able to see and to feel warm and secure from those he feared God took away their light extinguishing it the plural pronoun in nūrihim takes into account the plural import of alladhī; and left them in darkness unable to see what is around them confused as to the way in fear; likewise are those who have found temporary security by professing faith but who will meet with terror and punishment upon death; these last are. In the example related to fire, He compares them to someone who lights a fire to illuminate things, but when it is lit and he thinks he will benefit from its light, it goes out, smoldering and leaving him in the dark.

**Allah takes away their light.**

(Allah removed their light) means, Allah removed what benefits them, and this is the light, and He left them with what harms them, that is, the darkness and smoke. (And left them in darkness), that is their doubts, disbelief and hypocrisy. But when they die (Allah taketh away their light), the benefit of their [outward] faith, (and leaveth them in darkness) facing the hardships of the grave, (where they cannot see) any comfort. When it was revealed however they denied it and Allah took away their light, i.e. their desire to believe and the benefit of such belief. Such people then remain in the dark, unable to see anything or find a way.

**How the parable fits the hypocrites.**

Such is the case with the hypocrites who preferred misguidance over guidance, deviation over righteousness. This parable indicates that the hypocrites first believed, then disbelieved, just as Allah stated in other parts of the Qur'an. (Their likeness), the likeness of the hypocrites vis-�-vis Muhammad ﷺ (is as the likeness of one who kindleth fire), lights a fire in the darkness in order to provide safety for his family, property and person, (and when it sheddeth its light around him), when it sheds its light and he sees what is around him and feels secure, at that very moment the Fire is put out. Likewise, the hypocrites believed openly in Muhammad ﷺ as well as in the Qur'an and by doing so they felt their persons, families and properties were safe, avoiding in the process imprisonment or death. Similarly something of the benefits of this world appear to the hypocrites outwardly but then they are afflicted in the hereafter by the pain of the punishment. Or [it may be that] something of their affirmation iqrār flashes but then they remain in the darkness of their denial inkār.

**Two kinds of hypocrite, likened to two kinds of men.**

The last four verses bring out the miserable plight of the hypocrites with the help of two extended similes. The choice of two examples is meant to divide the hypocrites into two kinds of men. On the one hand were those in whom disbelief had taken deep roots, so that they had little inclination towards Islam, but pretended to be Muslims for worldly motives - the Holy Qur'an compares them to the man who, having found light, again loses it, and is left in darkness. On the other hand were those who did recognize the truth of Islam, and sometimes wished to be genuine Muslims, but worldly interests would not allow them to do so, and they remained in a perpetual state of hesitation and doubt - they have been likened to the men caught in a thunderstorm who move forward a step or two when there is a flash of lightning, but, when it is over, again get stuck. Allah shows us what the hypocrites are like with two examples: one related to fire, and the other to water.

**Another reading, about the Jews.**

It is also said this simile refers to the Jews. In this respect, the likeness of the Jews vis-�-vis Muhammad ﷺ is like a man who raises a flag in a lost battle and by doing so attracts other defeated fighters. But when they gather they put their flag down and, consequently, their benefit and safety immediately vanish. Similarly, the Jews used to say that Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an, prior to its revelation, would support them. This is because although they wanted to believe in Muhammad ﷺ they did not do so, and consequently they were left them in the error of Judaism, unable to see guidance.

**Too exalted to coin similitudes.**

Ibn 'Abbas said, according to the report of Abu Salih: When Allah, exalted is He, coined these two similitudes for the hypocrites - he means Allah's sayings (Their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindleth fire) [2:17] and (Or like a rainstorm from the sky .) [2:19] - they said: 'Allah is too exalted and sublime to coin similitudes'. When Allah mentioned gnats and spiders in His Book and used them to coin similitudes for the disbelievers, the Jews laughed and said: 'this does not resemble Allah's speech', and so Allah revealed this verse . Upon hearing this, they said: 'See how Allah mentions gnats and spiders in the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad; what is the use of this?' And so Allah revealed this .

18.text:
The verse completes the parable of the fire by naming the state the hypocrites are left in. "They are wilfully deaf, dumb, and blind" uses three words for the three ways guidance reaches a person and is shared. They are deaf, so they do not hear the truth in a way that lets them accept it. They are dumb, so they cannot speak the words that would benefit them, words of faith and of goodness. They are blind, so they do not see the path of guidance even when it is in front of them. The word wilfully marks that this is not a physical defect. Their ears, tongues and eyes work. It is their hearts that have gone deaf and blind, by their own choice, after they turned away from the light they had been given. "so they will never return to the Right Path" names the consequence. Someone who cannot hear the call, cannot speak of the truth and cannot see the road has no means of finding his way back. He is like the man in the parable whose fire went out, left in such darkness that he cannot get back to the state he was in before. The words do not deny that a person can repent. They describe the state of these people as long as they remain as they are, persisting in error and refusing to be held back from it. The verse is a warning to anyone who hears the truth and keeps putting it off, since the senses that were not used for guidance may one day stop answering when they are needed. The next verse gives the second parable, of people caught in a storm.

**Deaf, dumb and blind to the truth.**

deaf to the truth so that they cannot hear it and accept it; dumb mute as regards goodness unable to speak of it; and blind to the path of guidance so that they cannot perceive it; they shall not return from error. Further, this person could not hear or speak and became so blind that even if there were light, he would not be able to see. (dumb) and cannot utter the words that might benefit them,. They are deaf: unable to hear and accept the truth, or speak about it. They are blind to seeing the truth, so they do not turn back from their error.

**Blindness of the heart, not of the eyes.**

(Verily, it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts which are in the breasts that grow blind)(22:46) and this why they cannot get back to the state of guidance that they were in, since they sold it for misguidance. they could not see) meaning, they are unable to find the correct path or find its direction. deaf dumb blind they shall not return Deaf to hearing the calls of the Real with the ears of their hearts dumb to whispered conversation with the Real with the tongue of their innermost selves blind to witnessing the flow of decreed events with the eyes of their faculties of insight. It is said deaf to hearing through the Real dumb to speaking through the Real blind to studying creation through the Real.

**Why they will never return, or desist.**

(Deaf) pretending to be deaf, (dumb) pretending to be dumb, (and blind) pretending to be blind; (so they return not) from their disbelief and error. This is why he cannot return to the state that he was in before this happened to him. They shall not return from their persistent shamelessness nor can they be deterred from their wholehearted embrace of errors. There was no predetermination for them to desist iqlāʿ and no allotment to help them in being deterred irtidāʿ. In the course of these parables, the hypocrites have also been warned that they are not beyond the power of Allah, and that He can, as and when He likes, take away their sight and hearing, and even destroy them.
